newsitem.title: CHINA: Northern China region to inflate wind energy use.
newsitem.headline: Northern China region to inflate wind energy use.

text.p: Authorities in China's northern region of Inner Mongolia hope to boost the capacity of wind power generation by 12 times by the turn of the century, the Xinhua new agency said on Wednesday.
Authorities expected total wind generating capacity to reach 200 megawatts by 2000 from the existing 15 megawatts, it said.
They planned to increase the number of wind converters in the semi-arid region which has 125,000 generators, it said. It did not give details of the expected number of new generators.
Wind-power projects in the region have been funded locally as well as with government loans from Germany and Denmark, Xinhua said.

Power generated by wind could account for 1.5 percent of the region's annual total power output by the end of the century, Xinhua quoted Chen Tongmuo, a senior engineer with Inner Mongolia Wind Power Corp, as saying.
In 1995, Inner Mongolia generated 55,000 megawatt/hours of electricity from wind which accounted for 0.3 percent of the total power production, Xinhua said.
